text:
Tom E.: Hi folks, day 3 on Risk team. Blocked on a couple of observability bits for a postmortem: need a PNG export of panel 7 from grafana://dash/fraud-dashboard (for the doc), CSV timeseries export for the same panel, Datadog view for monitors tagged service:fraud, and Sentry access to fraud-prod. Email tom.e@redwood.ai. Who should I ping?
Jules (DevEx): Welcome Tom! :wave: Short path: Okta provisioning -> add to observability-viewers. If you need temporary edits or exports, file an identity request at https://go.redwood/identity-requests with scopes grafana:viewer (or grafana:export if we have that), datadog:standard, sentry:member and paste the ID here. For PNGs we prefer the render API or internal snapshots (no public links).
Tom E.: I can't find observability-viewers in Okta (My Groups shows only default groups). Filed request REQ-215678 with reason: need exports for postmortem doc + triage.
okta-bot: Request REQ-215678 created. Manager approval pending. Approve at https://idp.redwood/requests/215678
infra-bot: Datadog invite queued for tom.e@redwood.ai (expires in 48h). Invite ref: 1859001234-INV. Track at https://idp.redwood/invites/1859001234
Rahul (Platform): Hi Tom 44b Which org/namespace? Fraud dashboards live in /team/risk and sometimes in region-specific folders. Also for PNG/CSV you can use the Grafana render and panel API. Example commands:
```bash
# PNG render (panel snapshot)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GRAF_TOKEN" \
  "https://grafana.internal/render/d-solo/fraud-dashboard?panelId=7&width=1200&height=600" -o panel7.png

# Panel CSV export (time range last 1h)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GRAF_TOKEN" \
  "https://grafana.internal/api/datasources/proxy/1/query?db=metrics&q=SELECT+...&epoch=ms" -o panel7.csv
```
Rahul (Platform): If you prefer not to touch tokens I can generate the PNG and drop it in the team drive. Also who is your manager for approval?
Tom E.: Org: redwood-eu-risk. Manager is @Maya R. I've pinged her to approve the Okta request.
security-bot: Policy: EU access requires MFA + company-managed device + disk encryption. Enroll Okta Verify and confirm device at https://idp.redwood/devices before provisioning completes.
Tom E.: Enrolled Okta Verify and device registered.
okta-bot: Identity REQ-215678 status: approved. Provisioning starting.
Rahul (Platform): Provisioned Grafana view for /team/risk and Sentry invite resent. You should also be able to see Datadog monitors after the Datadog invite is accepted.
Tom E.: I can open the dashboard but I get a permission error when trying to use the render endpoint (403).
Rahul (Platform): That's because exports are controlled by a folder-level setting. I've temporarily enabled export for /team/risk and whitelisted your account. Try the render curl again.
Tom E.: Ran the render command and got panel7.png — perfect. CSV export also worked, got the timeseries. Thanks!
Tom E.: Datadog invite arrived and I can see monitors tagged service:fraud. Sentry invite still pending.
Marta (dash-owner): Hey @Tom E. 44b I own the fraud-dashboard. If you need long-term edit rights to add annotations for the postmortem please file a role change request or DM me the exact annotation text and time and I can add it for you. Also FYI we keep the alert runbook here: https://runbooks.redwood/risk/fraud-rate.
Tom E.: Can you add a timestamped annotation for the incident at 2024-08-12T09:12Z with note "spike during experiment"? I'll take the PNG/CSV for the doc.
Marta (dash-owner): Done, annotation posted and I added the panel PNG to the team drive under /shared/risk/postmortems.
infra-bot: Sentry invite sent to tom.e@redwood.ai. Invite ref: 1859001234-SNTY
Tom E.: Accepted Sentry and can see release-health for fraud-prod. All good now, thanks everyone :tada:
Jules (DevEx): Nice work. Quick tips: 1) use internal Grafana snapshots for docs instead of public exports, 2) for bulk exports we have a service account you can request via infra ticket, 3) if you need monitoring playbooks we keep a playlist at /playlists/risk-oncall.
Tom E.: Will follow up if we need the service account. Appreciate the quick help!
